stack_spec.name: Built with Spec4 (BWS4)
stack_spec.description: A unified web app that showcases Spec4 through a gallery of illustrative example apps demonstrating agentic AI patterns: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool-use, a visual embeddings explorer, a single-call (simple vs. structured-output) demo, a two-step chained-calls (role-played writer/critic) demo, a planning-agent trip-day planner demo, and an orchestrated-subagents demo in which a coordinator picks two specialists from a fixed roster, briefs them, runs them in parallel, and merges their answers.

languages.name: Python
languages.role: backend service — REST API, LiteLLM/OpenRouter orchestration, RAG pipeline, embeddings example app (embedding + PCA projection), single-call example app (simple/structured generation), chained-calls example app (two-step role-played generation via PydanticAI), planning-agent example app (planner/executor agents with tool-calling via PydanticAI, SSE streaming), orchestrated-subagents example app (coordinator delegation, concurrent knowledge-only specialists via asyncio.gather, merge, SSE streaming), shared framework services (generation, embedding, storage, usage limiting, content moderation), Neon/Postgres access

languages.name: TypeScript
languages.role: browser client — single-page app presenting the landing page and all example apps

targets.name: web_client
targets.purpose: the browser UI presenting the landing page and every example app (RAG, tool-use, embeddings, single-call, chained-calls, planning-agent, orchestrated-subagents, future patterns), with per-example-app code-splitting so the gallery can grow without bloating the initial load
targets.hosting: Render Static Site (free tier — no spin-down, served via CDN)
targets.build: Vite build producing a hashed static bundle with route-based lazy-loaded chunks per example app
targets.distribution: served at the app's root domain

targets.name: api
targets.purpose: serves the SPA's data needs — LiteLLM/OpenRouter orchestration, RAG pipeline (chunking, embedding, retrieval), embeddings example app (preconfigured/custom text embedding and 2D projection), single-call example app (simple text and structured/schema-conforming generation), chained-calls example app (two-step role-played generation via PydanticAI/OpenRouter), planning-agent example app (planner call, plan validation, tool-using executor calls streamed via server-sent events), orchestrated-subagents example app (moderation gate, coordinator delegation decision, two concurrent knowledge-only specialists, merged answer, all streamed via server-sent events), Exa search integration, and shared framework services (generation, embedding, storage, usage limiting, content moderation)
targets.runtime: Python 3.12 on a Render free Web Service (spins down after ~15 min idle; cold-starts on next request; 750 free instance-hours/month)
targets.build: container image or native Python buildpack from the repo
targets.api_contract: REST; OpenAPI schema auto-generated by FastAPI; the planning-agent run endpoint streams incremental JSON results (Plan, then StepResults, then Itinerary) as server-sent events over a POST request; the orchestrated-subagents run endpoint likewise streams the DelegationDecision, then per-specialist status/answer events as the concurrent specialist tasks complete, then the MergedAnswer, as server-sent events over a POST request

exposure.cors: allow only the web_client's own origin

capabilities.capability_class: a capable general-purpose free model for grounded, structured-output answers (meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free)
a fast alternate free model, also strong at structured/tool-oriented output (google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free)
a capable general-purpose free model able to produce both plain text and JSON-schema-conforming structured output for a single direct prompt/response demo (meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free)
a fast alternate free model, also strong at structured/JSON output, for the single-call demo

OpenRouter (via LiteLLM).fallback: Gemini 2.0 Flash free takes over automatically via LiteLLM routing if the primary Llama 3.3 70B free model's rate limit is hit or it errors, for both the RAG and single-call tiers

capabilities.capability_class: a capable general-purpose free model able to sustain a distinct role-played persona (struggling writer, harsh critic) across a two-step sequential chain (meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free)
a fast alternate free model, also strong at persona/role-played and structured JSON output, for the chained-calls demo

a capable free model with reliable native tool-calling and structured output, able to decompose a trip goal into a validated small plan and to execute research/synthesis steps against a web-search tool
a fast alternate free model, also capable of tool-calling and structured JSON output, for the planner and executor calls

a capable general-purpose free model with reliable structured output, able to (a) choose exactly two specialists from a fixed roster of four and write a distinct brief for each, (b) answer a briefed sub-question as a knowledge-only specialist with no tool access, and (c) merge two independent specialist answers into one integrated response
a fast alternate free model, also strong at structured JSON output, for the coordinator delegation call, either specialist call, or the merge call

structured-output generation of the disagreement note comparing the two specialist answers; produced as fields on the merge call's existing structured output rather than as an additional model call, so the run's three-call budget is unchanged

OpenRouter (via PydanticAI).fallback: Gemini 2.0 Flash free takes over automatically via PydanticAI's native FallbackModel if the primary Llama 3.3 70B free model errors or hits its rate limit — for either step of the chained-calls chain, for any planner or executor call of the planning-agent run, and for the coordinator delegation call, either specialist call, or the merge call of the orchestrated-subagents run; both models' slugs are read from the same shared model-slug config module used by the LiteLLM lane

integrations.name: Exa Search API
integrations.purpose: fetch ranked, real external search results (title, summary, source) so tool-use example apps can incorporate outside information, and serve as the model-invoked web-search tool for the planning-agent example app's research steps

integrations.name: OpenAI Moderation API (omni-moderation-latest)
integrations.purpose: pre-dispatch safety classification of visitor-supplied free-form questions (abuse, self-harm, sexual, hate, violence, illicit) before any coordinator call is made; chosen because the moderation endpoint is free of charge and does not consume the OpenRouter free-model allowance, so the orchestrated-subagents run's three-model-call budget is unaffected; exposed as a shared framework service so any future example app with a free-form input can reuse it, and invoked only for free-form input — curated preset questions are pre-vetted and skip it entirely
integrations.protocol: REST over HTTPS; POST /v1/moderations, called with httpx and parsed into a Pydantic ModerationVerdict
integrations.auth: API key; OPENAI_API_KEY (entered in the Render dashboard as a sync:false secret, as the OpenRouter and Exa keys are)

primary_store.purpose: durable relational store for everything the app writes, doubling as the vector index for the RAG example app
primary_store.durability: source of truth; survives restarts and redeploys, including Render's free-tier spin-down; Neon's free tier persists indefinitely (unlike Render's free Postgres, which expires after 30 days)

collections.name: usage_limits
physical: usage window column keyed to the current UTC hour (migrated from the previous per-UTC-day window; requires an Alembic revision on the existing usage-window schema, an update to the shared quota-check/logging function every example app calls, updated pytest coverage of the usage-window logic, and refusal copy reworded from 'daily' to 'hourly' across all example apps)
collections.purpose: the showcase-wide model/search allowance gate, enforced server-side before every provider call by every example app; now windowed per UTC hour rather than per UTC day, on the same clock as each app's own per-session run counter

collections.name: allowance_holds
collections.purpose: reserve/redeem/refund records against the showcase-wide hourly usage gate, so the orchestrated-subagents run's full three-call budget is held before the coordinator delegation call is made and a confirmed dispatch either completes or is refused up front with a clear reason; refunded when a run fails before spending its reserved calls
physical: index on capability and usage window

collections.name: moderation_log
collections.purpose: safety-gate telemetry for free-form question moderation: a salted hash of the question (never the raw text), the returned category, confidence, latency, and whether the call failed closed; satisfies the capability's privacy requirement that raw visitor question text is not retained
physical: salted question hash column; no raw question text column

embedding_projection_cache.choice: in-process NumPy array of preconfigured embeddings + fitted PCA model, held in memory (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 vectors, scikit-learn PCA)
embedding_projection_cache.purpose: fills the vector_index substrate for the embeddings example app's custom_text_semantic_placement capability: holds the preconfigured examples' embeddings and the fitted PCA projection so a new custom-text point can be transformed into the same stable 2D layout without recomputing it, and without persisting user-entered custom text beyond the request per the capability's privacy requirement
embedding_projection_cache.durability: ephemeral — rebuilt from bundled_assets' preconfigured_text_examples at process startup or on first request; ephemeral in-process derived state, rebuildable, not a source of truth; custom text embeddings exist only for the duration of the request and are never persisted

collections.name: preconfigured_example_embeddings
physical: in-process NumPy array, 384-dim (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) per preconfigured example
fitted PCA model held in memory, reused via .transform() for custom text

bundled_assets.choice: static content bundled at build time
bundled_assets.purpose: read-only content that only changes via a code change/redeploy, not user action

collections.name: preconfigured_text_examples
collections.purpose: the curated set of words, short phrases, and sentences spanning multiple categories used to seed the embeddings example app's plot

collections.name: preset_prompts
collections.purpose: the curated set of example prompts (e.g. summarize, classify, extract) with their labeled intent, offered as one-click choices in the single-call example app

collections.name: persona_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static system-prompt templates and few-shot exemplars defining the 'struggling writer' and 'harsh critic' personas used by the two chained calls; read-only, versioned in-repo alongside the RAG and single-call prompt conventions

collections.name: planning_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static system-prompt templates for the planning-agent example app: the planner prompt (goal decomposition into a bounded, validated plan of research + synthesis steps) and the synthesis prompt (composing the final one-day itinerary from step results); read-only, versioned in-repo following the same prompt-versioning convention as the other example apps

collections.name: specialist_roster_config
collections.purpose: the fixed roster of four knowledge-only specialists (Technical, Financial, Historical, Practical) with each one's id, display name, scope description, and column colour; read as the closed set the coordinator must choose exactly two from, and used to validate the delegation decision before it is shown to the visitor

collections.name: curated_presets
collections.purpose: curated preset questions, each with a preset id and its wording, chosen so different presets produce visibly different specialist pairings; preset questions are pre-vetted and therefore bypass the moderation gate that free-form questions pass through

collections.name: orchestration_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static system-prompt templates for the orchestrated-subagents example app: the coordinator delegation prompt (choose exactly two roster specialists, give a pairing rationale, write a distinct brief for each), the specialist prompt (answer only your own brief, knowledge-only, no tools), and the merge prompt (reconcile and integrate the two answers and note where they disagree); read-only, versioned in-repo following the same prompt-versioning convention as the other example apps

browser_local_storage.purpose: keeps small per-device visitor state across visits without a backend round trip, and keeps each example app's own demonstration run counter and prior results on the device so they survive navigating away and back
browser_local_storage.durability: persists per-device/browser only; not a source of truth, not shared across devices; resettable by the visitor — hard quota protection is always the server-side usage_limits gate plus per-run call ceilings, never this store

collections.name: run_allowance
collections.purpose: advisory per-session run counter and cap for the planning-agent example app, shown to the user with remaining runs; deliberately client-side only — hard quota protection remains the server-side usage_limits gate plus the fixed per-run call ceiling enforced by plan validation

collections.name: orchestrated_run_allowance
collections.purpose: the orchestrated-subagents example app's three-run session counter plus the visitor's own prior run records (delegation decision, per-specialist briefs, specialist answers, merged answer), stamped with the UTC hour so the counter resets on the same hourly clock as the server-side showcase-wide gate; persisting the records here is what lets the runs-remaining count and previously produced results survive navigating away and back with no server-side visitor identity at all, and hard quota protection remains the server-side usage_limits gate plus the reserved three-call budget

chunking_pipeline.choice: hand-rolled paragraph/fixed-window text splitter, in application code
chunking_pipeline.purpose: splits reference_dataset documents into passages before embedding; kept simple and transparent given the small curated dataset, serving the project's teaching-clarity goal

embedding_pipeline.choice: sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), in-process at index time and query time
embedding_pipeline.purpose: fills the catalog's embedding_pipeline substrate for both the RAG example (vectors written to and read from dataset_embeddings) and the embeddings example app (vectors for preconfigured examples and custom text, held in embedding_projection_cache) — the same shared embedding model is reused rather than introduced separately; the package itself is listed under libraries

retriever.choice: SQLAlchemy query using pgvector's cosine-distance operator against dataset_embeddings
retriever.purpose: finds the top-N passages most similar to a question's embedding, to ground the generated answer

pipeline_runner.choice: PydanticAI, using its OpenRouterProvider and native FallbackModel to run the fixed two-step 'struggling writer' → 'harsh critic' sequence, with the first call's response passed directly as the second call's input
pipeline_runner.purpose: fills the catalog's pipeline_runner substrate for the chained-calls example app; chosen over a hand-rolled function because upcoming example apps will coordinate multiple agents, and PydanticAI's typed Agent primitives extend naturally to that without a framework swap; the free-model slugs used by its OpenRouterProvider and FallbackModel are read from the same shared model-slug config module the LiteLLM lane uses, and the existing usage_limits/service_log_entries quota-check function gates calls on this path exactly as it gates the LiteLLM path

agent_loop_runtime.choice: PydanticAI agent runs (OpenRouterProvider + FallbackModel, slugs from the shared model-slug config), deliberately constrained: one structured-output planner call produces a Pydantic-validated Plan capped at 2–3 executor steps (trimmed or re-planned with a note if nonconforming), then executor steps run sequentially only after the user's explicit go-ahead, with the shared usage-limit gate checked before every model call and each result streamed to the client as it completes
agent_loop_runtime.purpose: fills the catalog's agent_loop_runtime substrate for the planning-agent example app; the 'loop' is visible, bounded, and user-advanced rather than autonomous, honoring the feature's human-in-the-loop mechanism, the per-run call ceiling (~1 planner + 2–3 executor calls), and the project's teaching-transparency goal; the PydanticAI package itself is listed under libraries

tool_execution_harness.choice: PydanticAI native tool-calling (tool registration on the executor agent) wrapping the existing Exa search client (httpx) as a typed web-search tool for research steps
tool_execution_harness.purpose: fills the catalog's tool_execution_harness substrate for the planning-agent example app, following the spec's tool protocol strategy: native model tool-calling, direct SDK-wrapped, no MCP; the run-allowance/quota check is a direct internal service-layer call, never a model-exposed tool, so the model cannot decide whether quota is spent; the PydanticAI package itself is listed under libraries

subagent_orchestration_runtime.choice: PydanticAI agents dispatched directly in-process and fanned out with asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True): one structured-output coordinator agent returns a Pydantic-validated DelegationDecision (exactly two specialist ids from the fixed four-name roster, a pairing rationale, and a distinct brief per specialist, re-requested once when validation fails), then after the visitor's explicit dispatch confirmation the two knowledge-only specialist agents run as concurrent async tasks, then the coordinator agent is called a third time to merge their answers
subagent_orchestration_runtime.purpose: fills the catalog's subagent_orchestration_runtime substrate for the orchestrated-subagents example app; chosen over PydanticAI agent delegation (specialists as coordinator tools) because a model-driven tool loop could not guarantee exactly three calls and would serialise the specialists, defeating the visible parallelism the demo teaches, and because the spec requires specialists to have no tool access — the tool protocol strategy specifies a DIRECT in-process call, one async task per selected specialist, gathered via the parallel_fanout mechanism; chosen over LangGraph to avoid a second agent framework and its state-graph/checkpointing machinery on Render's free tier; gathering with return_exceptions=True is what lets one specialist fail while the other column's answer stays on screen and the merge proceeds with a note about the missing contribution; the shared usage-limit gate is checked and the full three-call budget reserved before the coordinator call, and the PydanticAI package itself is listed under libraries

ai_conventions.prompt_versioning: the rag_example_app's prompt template (including its structured-output schema/instructions) is stored as a versioned file in-repo (e.g. backend/app/rag/prompts/answer_v1.md), tagged with a semantic version in the filename/header, and loaded by a thin resolver function; the single_call_example_app's preset prompts follow the same convention — plain text/intent metadata stored in-repo (e.g. backend/app/single_call/prompts/presets.py or a versioned data file), with any structured-mode JSON schemas defined alongside as versioned Pydantic models; the chained_calls_example_app's 'struggling writer' and 'harsh critic' persona system-prompt templates follow the identical convention — versioned files under backend/app/chained_calls/prompts/ (e.g. writer_v1.md, critic_v1.md), loaded by the same thin resolver pattern; the planning_agent_example_app's planner and synthesis prompt templates follow the identical convention — versioned files under backend/app/planning/prompts/ (e.g. planner_v1.md, synthesis_v1.md), with the Plan/StepResult/Itinerary structured-output schemas defined alongside as versioned Pydantic models; the orchestrated_subagents_example_app's coordinator delegation, specialist, and merge prompt templates follow the identical convention — versioned files under backend/app/orchestrated/prompts/ (e.g. delegation_v1.md, specialist_v1.md, merge_v1.md), with the DelegationDecision/Brief/SubagentResult/MergedAnswer structured-output schemas (the merged answer carrying the disagreement note as fields on the same schema) defined alongside as versioned Pydantic models; no external prompt-management tool

libraries.name: FastAPI
libraries.purpose: REST API framework, async-native, generates OpenAPI schema from Pydantic models

libraries.name: SQLAlchemy
libraries.purpose: ORM/toolkit for Neon Postgres access, including pgvector column types

libraries.name: asyncpg
libraries.purpose: async PostgreSQL driver used by SQLAlchemy's async engine to connect to Neon

libraries.name: Alembic
libraries.purpose: versioned schema migrations for the Postgres/Neon schema, including the revision migrating the shared usage-limit window from per-UTC-day to per-UTC-hour and the revisions adding allowance_holds and moderation_log

libraries.name: httpx
libraries.purpose: async HTTP client for calling the Exa Search API without blocking the event loop (tool-use example app and the planning-agent example app's web-search tool), and for the shared moderation service's POST to the OpenAI Moderation endpoint, following the same thin-client pattern as the Exa client

libraries.name: Pydantic
libraries.purpose: request/response validation, structured-output schema for the RAG answer format, per-preset schema models for the single-call example app's Structured mode, the Plan/PlanStep/StepResult/Itinerary schemas bounding the planning-agent run, the DelegationDecision/Brief/SubagentResult/MergedAnswer schemas that constrain the coordinator to exactly two roster specialists with distinct briefs and carry the disagreement note on the merge output, and the ModerationVerdict model the shared moderation service parses the OpenAI moderation response into

libraries.name: LiteLLM
libraries.purpose: unified interface to OpenRouter's free models for text generation, with built-in retry/fallback across the primary and fallback model, used by RAG and by the single-call example app's simple and structured-output requests

libraries.name: PydanticAI
libraries.purpose: agent framework running the chained-calls example app's fixed two-step writer→critic sequence, the planning-agent example app's planner/executor agents (structured-output planner, native tool-calling executors wrapping the Exa search tool), and the orchestrated-subagents example app's coordinator and two knowledge-only specialist agents (structured-output delegation, concurrent in-process specialist runs gathered with asyncio, structured-output merge), all via its OpenRouterProvider and native FallbackModel; the anticipated multi-agent growth path realized with no framework swap

libraries.name: sse-starlette
libraries.purpose: server-sent events response support for FastAPI, streaming the planning-agent run's incremental results (Plan, each StepResult, the Itinerary) and the orchestrated-subagents run's three phases (DelegationDecision, then per-specialist status/answer events as the concurrent tasks complete, then the MergedAnswer), with built-in ping/keep-alive (important behind Render's proxy) and client-disconnect detection so an abandoned run stops spending model quota

libraries.name: tenacity
libraries.purpose: bounded retry with backoff around outbound calls, including the shared moderation service's call to the OpenAI moderation endpoint before it fails closed

libraries.name: sentence-transformers
libraries.purpose: in-process local embedding model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) for text representation at index and query time, shared by the RAG pipeline and the embeddings example app so both use the same embedding representation

libraries.name: scikit-learn
libraries.purpose: PCA dimensionality reduction, fitted once on the preconfigured examples' embeddings and reused via .transform() for custom text, so the 2D layout stays stable across recalculations rather than jumping when a new point is added

libraries.name: numpy
libraries.purpose: numeric array support underpinning the embedding and PCA projection maths and the in-process projection cache

libraries.name: pgvector
libraries.purpose: Python/SQLAlchemy client for the pgvector Postgres extension, enabling vector columns and similarity queries

libraries.name: pydantic-settings
libraries.purpose: typed, validated configuration objects reading env vars/.env files (OpenRouter, Exa and OpenAI moderation keys, DB URL, CORS origin, Sentry DSN)

libraries.name: structlog
libraries.purpose: structured JSON logging for application events and service-log entries, including per-run orchestration telemetry (pairing distribution by preset, brief distinctness, merge behaviour) and moderation-gate telemetry

libraries.name: sentry-sdk
libraries.purpose: backend error tracking and aggregation across FastAPI, LiteLLM, PydanticAI, Exa and moderation calls, with model-call performance spans (token usage, latency, error rates) on the free tier

libraries.name: pytest
libraries.purpose: backend test runner

libraries.name: Ruff
libraries.purpose: Python linter and formatter; must be added to the dev dependency group, which currently omits it despite Ruff-specific suppressions already present in the backend source

libraries.name: mypy
libraries.purpose: strict static type checking of the comprehensively annotated backend, which currently has no configured type checker

libraries.name: React
libraries.purpose: UI framework for the single-page app

libraries.name: Vite
libraries.purpose: frontend build tool and dev server, with native code-splitting support

libraries.name: React Router
libraries.purpose: client-side routing with lazy-loaded routes, one per example app

libraries.name: TanStack Query
libraries.purpose: data fetching, caching, and loading/error state management for calls to the API

libraries.name: @microsoft/fetch-event-source
libraries.purpose: fetch-based SSE client supporting POST bodies, custom headers, and abort — required because the browser's native EventSource is GET-only and both the planning-agent run and the orchestrated-subagents run start from a POST payload; consumes the streamed Plan/StepResult/Itinerary events and the DelegationDecision/per-specialist status/MergedAnswer events, rendering each as it arrives so both parallel specialist columns are visibly in progress together

libraries.name: Tailwind CSS
libraries.purpose: utility-first styling enforcing a consistent visual language and light/dark theming across all example apps, including the single-call app's JSON displays and the orchestrated-subagents app's parallel specialist columns and rendered markdown

libraries.name: react-markdown
libraries.purpose: renders the orchestrated-subagents example app's markdown merged answer and the two specialist answers as React elements rather than via dangerouslySetInnerHTML, so model output derived from visitor free-form input cannot inject HTML or script on this unauthenticated public surface; confined to the app's lazy-loaded chunk and reusable by future example apps that display model prose

libraries.name: remark-gfm
libraries.purpose: adds GitHub-flavoured markdown support (tables, strikethrough) to react-markdown for specialist and merged answers that use them

libraries.name: plotly.js
libraries.purpose: core charting engine rendering the embeddings example app's interactive 2D scatter plot, with built-in hover, legend, and zoom/pan for the educational visualization

libraries.name: react-plotly.js
libraries.purpose: React component wrapper around plotly.js used to render the embeddings scatter plot declaratively, ships its own TypeScript declarations

libraries.name: Vitest
libraries.purpose: frontend unit/component test runner, Vite-native

libraries.name: React Testing Library
libraries.purpose: component testing focused on user-visible behavior

libraries.name: Playwright
libraries.purpose: end-to-end browser testing of full user flows across the deployed SPA and API

libraries.name: @sentry/react
libraries.purpose: frontend error tracking for unhandled exceptions and failed requests, unified with the backend Sentry project (free tier)

project_structure.purpose: FastAPI routers, one module per feature (landing, RAG, tool-use, embeddings, single-call, chained-calls, planning-agent, orchestrated-subagents, shared services, health)

shared framework services: LLM access (LiteLLM wrapper), embedding (sentence-transformers wrapper), storage abstraction, shared model-slug config, and the usage-limit quota-check/logging function — now windowed per UTC hour and extended with reserve/redeem/refund holds — reused by both the LiteLLM and PydanticAI call paths

shared content-moderation service: a generic moderate(text, calling_context) -> ModerationVerdict function calling the OpenAI moderation endpoint over httpx with tenacity-bounded retry, failing closed with a plain-language visitor message, logging only a salted hash of the input, and injected via FastAPI Depends so any example app with a free-form input can reuse it
RAG-specific logic: chunking pipeline, retriever, versioned prompt templates
embeddings example app logic: bundled preconfigured TextSample set, in-process embedding + PCA fit/transform, and the API route accepting custom text and returning the recalculated 2D projection

single-call example app logic: bundled preset prompt set, per-preset Pydantic schema models for Structured mode, and the API route returning a plain-text or structured (request+response) result via the shared LiteLLM generation service
chained-calls example app logic: PydanticAI agent setup, the two-step writer→critic run function, and the API route returning the intermediate and final outputs
versioned persona system-prompt templates ('struggling writer', 'harsh critic') following the project's in-repo prompt-versioning convention

planning-agent example app logic: PydanticAI planner agent (structured-output Plan, validated and trimmed to the 2–3 step cap), Exa web-search tool registration for executor agents, the sequential user-advanced executor run function gated by the shared quota check, and the SSE route streaming Plan, StepResults, and the final Itinerary
versioned planner and synthesis prompt templates with the Plan/StepResult/Itinerary structured-output Pydantic schemas alongside

orchestrated-subagents example app logic: the bundled four-specialist roster config and curated preset questions, the moderation gate call for free-form questions only, the PydanticAI coordinator agent producing a validated DelegationDecision (exactly two roster specialists with distinct briefs, re-requested once on violation), the asyncio.gather fan-out running the two knowledge-only specialist agents concurrently with return_exceptions=True, the merge call producing the MergedAnswer with its disagreement note, the three-call budget reservation against the shared hourly usage gate, and the SSE route streaming the delegation decision, per-specialist status/answers, and the merged answer

versioned coordinator delegation, specialist, and merge prompt templates with the DelegationDecision/Brief/SubagentResult/MergedAnswer structured-output Pydantic schemas alongside, following the project's in-repo prompt-versioning convention
SQLAlchemy models, session factory, Alembic migrations (including the per-UTC-hour usage-window migration and the allowance_holds and moderation_log additions)
configuration (pydantic-settings), logging/Sentry setup

pytest suites mirroring the package layout, including updated coverage of the hourly usage-window logic and new coverage of the delegation validator, the concurrent specialist fan-out, and the moderation service's fail-closed path

one folder per screen: landing, RAG example, tool-use example, embeddings example, single-call example, chained-calls example, planning-agent example, orchestrated-subagents example, framework console
one folder per example app (rag, tool-use, embeddings, single-call, chained-calls, planning, orchestrated, and future additions), each lazy-loaded via its own route
the embeddings example app's route module: plot component (react-plotly.js), custom-text input, and the educational explanation of the embedding pattern

the single-call example app's route module: prompt input and preset selector, Simple/Structured mode toggle, plain-text response view, side-by-side structured request/response JSON view, and the educational explanation of the single-call pattern

the chained-calls example app's route module: initial-request input, upfront description of each call's role, labeled intermediate-output and final-output blocks, the two-call quota-conservation notice, and the educational explanation of the chained-calls pattern

the planning-agent example app's route module: city/interests input, plan display, the explicit 'Next' advance button, progressively appearing step results consumed from the SSE stream, the final itinerary view, the localStorage-backed run-allowance display, the per-run and per-session limit notices, and the educational explanation of the planning-agent pattern

the orchestrated-subagents example app's route module: preset selector and free-form question input with the moderation refusal message, the delegation-decision panel (chosen pair, rationale, and each specialist's brief), the explicit 'Next' dispatch button, two parallel specialist columns each headed by its brief with live independent status, the merged answer and disagreement note rendered via react-markdown, the visible runs-remaining counter backed by the hour-stamped localStorage record with prior run records rehydrated on return, the disabled-input state with messaging that distinguishes this app's three-run session limit from the showcase-wide hourly allowance, and the educational explanation of the orchestrated-subagents pattern
shared UI: nav bar, theme toggle, layout shell, and the shared markdown renderer wrapper around react-markdown with its Tailwind typography styles
typed API client and TanStack Query hooks calling the backend, plus the SSE consumption hooks for the planning-agent and orchestrated-subagents run streams
route configuration with lazy (React.lazy) imports per example app
Vitest + React Testing Library suites

patterns: functional core / imperative shell — pure functions for chunking/retrieval/scoring logic, PCA fit/transform, single-call schema validation, the chained-calls writer→critic sequencing, the planning-agent plan validation/trimming and step sequencing, the orchestrated-subagents delegation validation (roster membership, exactly-two selection, brief distinctness) and the OpenAI-moderation-response-to-ModerationVerdict mapping, with thin FastAPI route handlers as the imperative shell

dependency injection for shared services (LiteLLM client, PydanticAI agents, DB session, Exa client, moderation service) via FastAPI's Depends, so tests can substitute them through app.dependency_overrides

concurrent subagent work is dispatched in application code with asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True) rather than delegated to a model-driven tool loop, so call counts stay fixed and one worker's failure never cancels the other
React: function components and hooks only, no class components
custom hooks for shared frontend logic (e.g. useExampleApps, useTheme, useRunAllowance)
documentation: Google-style docstrings on every public Python function
JSDoc on every exported TypeScript function
every source file, Python and TypeScript, opens with the header comment 'Built with Spec4 AI - https://spec4.ai'
